title: Pani Puri with Mint Water and Tamarind Water
summary: Crisp puri shells filled with spiced potato and chickpeas, topped up with a fiery, chilled mint-coriander water and a sweet tamarind water, and eaten in one bite.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: plus a few spare, as some break

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Break the tamarind into the hot water and leave for 30 minutes to soften.

steps.title: Herbs
steps.text: Blend the mint, coriander, ginger, chillies, lemon juice, cumin, chaat masala, salt, sugar and 250 ml of the cold water for 1-2 minutes, until very smooth.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through a fine sieve into a jug, pressing on the pulp, then stir in the remaining 500 ml cold water. Chill until serving; the colder it is, the more refreshing.

steps.title: Tamarind
steps.text: Squeeze the soaked tamarind with your fingers to loosen the pulp, then push it through the sieve into a bowl and discard the seeds and fibres. Stir in the jaggery, cumin, chilli powder, salt and the 250 ml cold water until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in unsalted water for 12-15 minutes, until tender. Drain, cool for 10 minutes, then crush roughly with the chaat masala, cumin, chilli powder and salt.

steps.title: Chickpeas
steps.text: Crush the chickpeas lightly with a fork and toss with the chaat masala.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Set out the puris, fillings and both waters. To eat, crack a small hole in the thin top of a puri, add a little potato and chickpea, fill with mint water and tamarind water to taste and eat in one bite.

tips: Taste the mint water before serving: add more chaat masala for tang or lemon for sharpness.
If the puris feel soft, crisp them at 180 °C for 3-4 minutes and cool.
Let everyone build their own; a filled puri goes soggy fast.
storage: The mint water keeps for 1 day and the tamarind water for 1 week in the fridge. The fillings keep for 2 days. Store the puris airtight at room temperature. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
